title: MCLR: Improving Conditional Modeling via Inter-Class Likelihood-Ratio Maximization and Unifying Classifier-Free Guidance with Alignment Objectives
abstract: arXiv:2603.22364v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Diffusion models achieve strong generative performance but often rely on classifier-free guidance (CFG), an inference-time intervention that modifies the sampling trajectory. Since standard denoising score matching (DSM) should recover the target distribution when the score is learned accurately, the practical necessity of CFG suggests deficiencies in learned conditional scores. We identify weak inter-class separation as one such limitation: samples generated from the same noise under different labels can retain similar class-agnostic structure. To address this deficiency, we introduce MCLR, a principled fine-tuning objective that explicitly maximizes inter-class likelihood-ratios, thereby strengthening class-specific structures under standard sampling. tldr: 本文提出MCLR微调目标，通过显式最大化类间似然比来强化类特定结构，从而在不依赖无分类器引导的情况下显著提升扩散模型的条件生成能力，并缩小了与CFG的差距。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes MCLR, a principled fine-tuning objective that explicitly maximizes inter-class likelihood-ratios to strengthen class-specific structures, substantially improving guidance-free conditional generation in diffusion models and narrowing the gap to classifier-free guidance.
